existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 CapabilityStatement has local breaking changes: duplicate REST modes are now an error and `patchFormat` is narrowed. The top migration concerns are REST block normalization, enum/type updates for resource and interaction metadata, and lossy R6-to-R4 conversion for new version/resource/capability content. The main uncertainty is semantic intent in narrative-only conformance text.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should combine structural normalization with terminology review. R4 producers should merge duplicate `rest` blocks by mode and validate `patchFormat` against the R6 patch MIME set. R6 consumers should regenerate models for `rest.resource.type` as `uri`, add new interaction/search/version enum values, and decide how to preserve R6-only optional elements when exporting to R4. Conformance processors should revisit import flattening and profile hierarchy checks.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for computable StructureDefinition differences, element additions, type changes, cardinality checks, and locally composed terminology comparisons. Confidence is medium for narrative-only semantic changes because the local inputs did not include official diff notes or narrative spec pages. Terminology confidence for BCP-13/all-language/extended-resource expansions is limited by lack of a terminology server expansion, but the material findings are supported by value set compose and CodeSystem evidence.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
CapabilityStatement keeps its resource identity. The aggregate has 2 hard R4-to-R6 instance break(s), 0 potential hard break(s), 1 non-mechanical migration finding(s), and 6 direct behavior/API finding(s).

R4 maturity context is normative/FMM 5, which creates strong stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 45/100, producing migration shape `moderate-targeted-remodel`, major migration `Partial`, and compatibility posture `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`.

10 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Expect targeted migration work, but continue reviewing individual breaks. Because R4 stability pressure is strong, low-cost compatible designs should be preferred unless they clearly undermine the R6 goal.

topFindings.title: R6 adds an error invariant requiring only one REST block per mode
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 instance with two `rest` repetitions both using `mode = server` or both using `mode = client` becomes invalid under R6 `cpb-4`.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: patchFormat required binding narrows from general MIME types to a patch-specific value set
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 allowed any valid MIME type in `patchFormat`; R6 rejects values outside the five patch MIME codes.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Mandatory fhirVersion can carry R5/R6 codes not allowed by R4
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 instance using `fhirVersion = 4.0.1` fails R6 required-binding validation; R6-to-R4 loss also occurs for R6 release-family codes such as `6.0`.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.
